title: Audit event diff serialization, retention & fast lookup strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a single pragmatic approach for serializing audit event deltas (diffs), applying retention and sampling, and enabling low-latency lookups for security/admin investigations. This ticket converges design decisions across RBAC v2, SSO/SAML flows, and admin control actions so that audit consumers (secops, support, compliance) can reconstruct actor/target changes accurately and efficiently.
background: We currently emit full audit blobs for many control-plane operations which increases storage cost and slows query performance for common investigations (e.g., who granted role X, what changed on a user object over 24h). Prior work (ENG-31288, ENG-24012) standardized event envelopes but left open: best diff encoding, how to reconcile actor/target canonical ids from SSO/SAML, and retention/sampling policy trade-offs for older diffs.
proposed_schema_summary: Event envelope with these top-level fields: event_id, timestamp, event_type, actor_canonical_id, actor_provider, target_canonical_id, target_type, change_kind (create|update|delete|permission-change|auth), diff_encoding, diff_payload, context (route/tenant), outcome, request_id, related_request_ids. diff_payload will be either compact JSON Patch or a protobuf-based delta depending on the encoding selection. All canonical ids must reference the identity registry (id:provider) to enable joins without duplicating PII.
diff_encoding_options: JSON Patch (RFC 6902) -- human readable, easy to debug, smaller for sparse changes
Protobuf delta (custom) -- binary, schema-evolution-friendly, smaller for repeated numeric fields
JSON-LD + provenance tags -- friendly for graph queries but verbose
Field-level redactable JSON with typed op list -- compromise: structured, easy to redact/transform
recommended_encoding: Field-level redactable JSON op list: an ordered list of ops {op, path, before, after, meta} where meta includes type and source. Rationale: balances readability for auditors, predictable size growth, and supports server-side redaction and compression. We will version the encoding (diff_encoding = v1) and provide a migration path to protobuf binary if compression proves necessary.
actor_target_resolution: Canonical IDs must be resolved at event emission time by consulting the identity registry cache. For SSO/SAML flows include both ephemeral session_subject (SAML NameID) and canonical_user_id (identity-registry id). For foreign identities (external IdPs) include provider tag and external_id. If canonical resolution fails, emit a tombstone reference with reason='unresolved_identity' and route to a reconciliation queue.
storage_and_indexing: Store raw event envelope in object storage (compressed) and a denormalized index in Elastic/ClickHouse for frequently queried fields: timestamp, event_type, actor_canonical_id, target_canonical_id, change_kind, request_id, outcome. Index also stores a small provenance summary (first N ops) to allow initial triage without decompressing.
retention_policy: Hot index: 365 days for denormalized index (configurable per tenant by SLA). Cold archive: full compressed envelopes retained for 7 years for enterprise/compliance customers, 90 days for standard tenants. Differential retention: critical security events (auth-failure, permission-change, admin-login) are retained longer in hot index. We will implement automated tiering and legal-hold flags.
privacy_and_compliance: PII fields (email, full_name, raw SAML assertions) must be redacted at emission time unless tenant has explicit opt-in. Use pseudonymization: store hashed_email and canonical_id; keep raw PII only in encrypted envelope and only where allowed by policy. Add audit markers for redaction so investigations can request unredacted data with approval.
query_performance_budget: Target 95th percentile query latency for common lookups (actor->events, target->changes) under 300ms for last 30 days on standard clusters. Use partitioning by date and tenant and precomputed reverse indexes for high-cardinality actors.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement encoder/decoder libraries (Go/TS) and unit tests. 2) Emit dual-mode for 4 weeks: both old full-blob and new diff payloads to evaluate size reduction and fidelity. 3) Migrate consumers (audit-ui, secops-alerts, retention jobs). 4) Flip producers to single-mode and enable cold-tiering. 5) Monitor metrics and run a post-mortem.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: unresolved identities lead to noisy events. Mitigation: reconciliation queue + metrics + backfill job
Risk: diffs incompatible with older consumers. Mitigation: versioned encoding + dual-write + decoder shim library
Risk: redaction mistakes leak PII. Mitigation: schema-level redaction hooks + automated tests + security review
acceptance_criteria: Encoder/decoder libraries in monorepo with >90% unit coverage
Dual-write mode emits both full_blob and diff_payload for all control-plane audit events
Storage cost reduction measured: projected 40% lower compressed volume for first 60d
Index query latency targets met in staging for 30d lookback
Security review completed and approved by Compliance
Documentation for incident playbook and reconciliation flows published
